_meta.indication: TRYVIO, in combination with other antihypertensive drugs, is indicated for the treatment of hypertension, to lower blood pressure in adult patients who are not adequately controlled on other drugs.

pivotal_trials.design: Multipart, multicenter study with a 4-week placebo run-in, followed by a 4-week double-blind, placebo-controlled treatment period in which 730 subjects were randomized 1:1:1 to aprocitentan 12.5 mg, 25 mg, or placebo (Part 1); a 32-week single-blind period on aprocitentan 25 mg (Part 2); and a double-blind randomized-withdrawal period to aprocitentan 25 mg or placebo (Part 3).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with uncontrolled BP (SBP ≥ 140 mmHg) despite being prescribed at least three antihypertensive medications.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: change in sitting SBP (SiSBP) from baseline to Week 4 during Part 1, measured at trough by unattended automated office blood pressure (uAOBP).
pivotal_trials.n: 730 subjects randomized 1:1:1 in Part 1; the primary efficacy analysis compared aprocitentan 12.5 mg (N=243) with placebo (N=244).
pivotal_trials.result: TRYVIO 12.5 mg was statistically superior to placebo in reducing SiSBP at Week 4: LS mean change -15.4 mmHg vs -11.6 mmHg (difference to placebo -3.8 mmHg; 97.5% CL -6.8, -0.8; p=0.0043).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2% and more frequent than placebo) were edema/fluid retention (9.1% vs 2.1% placebo) and anemia (3.7% vs 0% placebo) during the 4-week double-blind Part 1. A hemoglobin decrease >2 g/dL from baseline occurred in 7% of patients vs 1% of placebo. ERAs, including TRYVIO, carry risks of hepatotoxicity, fluid retention, hemoglobin decrease, and decreased sperm counts.
target_moa: Aprocitentan is an orally active, dual endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA) that inhibits the binding of endothelin (ET)-1 to ET_A and ET_B receptors; ET-1 signaling mediates vasoconstriction, fibrosis, cell proliferation and inflammation and has been implicated in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
modality: Small molecule (orally active dual endothelin receptor antagonist).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — TRYVIO can cause major birth defects if used by pregnant patients and is contraindicated in pregnancy. Exclude pregnancy prior to initiation, monthly during treatment, and for one month after stopping; use acceptable contraception; available only through the TRYVIO REMS.

rems.type: TRYVIO is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the TRYVIO REMS because of the risk of embryo-fetal toxicity; prescribers and pharmacies must be certified/enrolled.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee; it did not raise significant public health questions and outside expertise was not necessary.

summary.text: TRYVIO received traditional (standard) approval via a standard-review NDA (217686). The Agency accepts blood pressure lowering as a validated surrogate endpoint and basis for traditional approval of antihypertensive agents; efficacy was shown in the Phase 3 PRECISION study. Because of the risk of embryo-fetal toxicity, aprocitentan is available only through a restricted distribution program under a REMS, and a postmarketing requirement for a descriptive study of pregnancy outcomes was mandated.

In addition to the REMS, the risk will be included in labeling as a Boxed Warning and approval will include a postmarketing requirement for a descriptive study of pregnancy outcomes.
In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Tryvio (aprocitentan) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of embryo-fetal toxicity.

requirement.text: 4600-1 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Tryvio (aprocitentan) during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol.
